A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same joint sample/feature hierarchy-learning work, despite the changed title and algorithm names. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original sparse-approximation, classification, graph-learning and gene-expression clustering results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds synthetic hierarchy experiments and component comparisons in Appendices F and G.

M1.justification: Core alternating tree/TWD learning remains. V2 Algorithm 2 starts from Mr/Mc and filters before each TWD update, revising v1's initial-TWD/pre-filtering sequence. Algorithm 4 adds a variant that fixes the supplied sample distance during filtering and reference computations (Appendix F.12).

E1.justification: V2 adds synthetic user-video data for hierarchy recovery, sparse approximation and user/video classification (Appendix F.1). The original document, single-cell, graph and cancer/leukemia datasets remain.

E2.justification: Tree-WSV joins the main sparsity/classification and appendix clustering comparisons. V2 also evaluates wavelet-augmented TWD baselines and additional HGCN, post-hoc and Laplacian controls. Separate unregularized QUE/WSV clustering entries disappear.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix D.4 explicitly applies the training/test split to both tree learning and kNN; v2 Appendix E.4 instead describes partitioning the learned TWD matrix. V2 also replaces the matrix L1 sparsity description with explicit sample/feature averages and adds synthetic, initialization and fixed-hierarchy control protocols. These revise the documented evaluation design without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a synthetic hierarchy/noise case, strong-regularization initialization tests, wavelet controls for other TWDs and HGCNs, post-hoc versus iterative filtering, fixed-hierarchy tests and Laplacian filtering (Appendices F and G.2). The proposed method's clustering regularization ablation is replaced by an Algorithm 1/2 comparison.

E5.justification: V2 reports three random initializations per algorithm in Figure 7 and adds plus/minus values to the Sinkhorn comparison in Table 11. Conversely, Appendix F.11 drops v1's explicit statement that clustering means and standard deviations use ten runs. The main five-trial classification and ten-split graph practices remain.

E6.justification: Retained entries in main Tables 1–3 keep their scores, while v2 adds Tree-WSV, synthetic and extensive ablation results. The clustering comparison changes: v1's CoHSL breast-cancer/leukemia accuracies of 87.2/81.2 reappear under Algorithm 2, while Algorithm 1 has newly reported 85.6/75.8 values (v2 Table 12).

T1.justification: V2 removes the explicit least-squares objective and descent argument. Appendix C rewrites the convergence proofs around a tree-decoding separation condition, non-expansiveness and Opial's lemma, revises the diffusion-distance bound derivation, and introduces soft-thresholding reasoning into Theorem 2's proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: unsupervised joint sample/feature hierarchies through TWD, Haar filtering, convergence, and benefits for classification and HGCNs. Retitling and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine those claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations for adaptive Haar filtering, its advantages over Laplacian filtering, and why filtering arbitrary trees may fail. It qualifies strong-regularization uniqueness as potentially producing uninformative hierarchies and makes the existing geometric applicability limits more explicit.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies regularization/threshold search grids, the landmark exponent 0.1, handling of negative filtered values and synthetic-data generation details. Conversely, the earlier Sinkhorn parameter grid and Word2Vec access footnote are removed. Much of the original implementation information remains.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendices B/G.3 substantially expand positioning against WSV and newly cited Tree-WSV, distinguishing hierarchical representation learning from ground-metric approximation. The earlier biclustering contrast is dropped, and wavelet/graph-signal-processing connections expand. Lin et al. 2024a/2025 refers to the same underlying tree-construction work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background and method exposition are extensively rewritten, and CoHSL/CoHSL-Wavelet become Algorithm 1/2. The supplement gains a roadmap and is reorganized into separate integration, experimental-detail, analysis and discussion appendices.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and relocated, algorithms and figures are integrated with surrounding text, and new hierarchy plots and comparison tables are added. The clustering table is transposed, initial/iterative classification results are consolidated in Table 6, and v1's Sinkhorn bar chart becomes Table 11.

improvement.justification: Tree-WSV comparisons and targeted filtering controls strengthen the evidence for the method, while added parameter details and clearer diagrams improve usability. These gains are limited by unreconciled protocol/result-label changes and an overstatement in Table 12's discussion: Algorithm 1's Leukemia accuracy is 75.8, below BCOTλ's 80.9, despite the claim that both proposed variants outperform all baselines.
